steps.title: Compare unloaded boundary conditions
steps.explanation: Start at unit height with shear modulus 1500 Pa and bulk modulus 50000 Pa. Neither free sides nor unilateral walls need a reaction in the reference state.
steps.observe: Both J values and lateral stretch are 1; plate forces and wall reaction are zero.

steps.title: Impose the same height reduction
steps.explanation: Shorten height to 0.8. The free specimen solves zero lateral traction and expands sideways; the confined specimen is prevented from widening.
steps.observe: Free lateral stretch is about 1.11463 and J is 0.993914, compared with confined J=0.8. Plate forces are about 4.53637 N and 42.0887 N, respectively.

steps.title: Change bulk stiffness without changing height
steps.explanation: Increase bulk modulus fivefold while keeping the same geometry, shear modulus and boundary conditions. The free specimen can preserve more volume by expanding; the walls prevent that route.
steps.observe: Free J rises to about 0.998781 and plate force to 4.56728 N. Confined J stays 0.8 while its force rises to 202.089 N; stiffness does not override the prescribed walls.

steps.title: Read the residual before trusting a shape
steps.explanation: Return to bulk modulus 50000 Pa but stop bisection after eight iterations. The specimen still has positive volume and looks plausible, yet its free-side traction is not balanced.
steps.observe: Free lateral residual is about 24.0254 Pa, above the unchanged 0.00001 Pa criterion, so Free converged is false. Increase the cap manually to 64 to recover the second step.

audit.finding: Height-only controls hid bulk stiffness and root failure; a plausible finite iterate had no convergence status.
audit.change: Expose bulk modulus, bisection cap, plate forces, residual criterion and true convergence alongside free/confined geometry.
audit.remaining: One lateral degree of freedom in a homogeneous elastic ansatz. No unrestricted 3D stability, friction, plasticity, physiological calibration or tissue failure prediction.
